newsitem.title: UK: New business brisker on sugar freight market.
newsitem.headline: New business brisker on sugar freight market.

text.p: The sugar freight market saw a spate of new inquiry on Tuesday with offtake expected to be boosted shortly as a result of deliveries against New York's October futures contract, shipbrokers said.
A number of orders should soon emerge for north and south Brazil as origins after Monday's expiry, they said.
Market sources in London said trade house E D & F Man was the receiver of more than 4,000 lots of raw sugar from four different deliverers, using the ports of Santos, Paranagua, Maceio and Recife.
The New York exchange has yet to confirm the expiry details.
New business quoted on Tuesday included Mauritius Sugar Syndicate (MSS), open for 17,500/17,750 tonnes of bulk sugar from Port Louis to London for 21/24 October.
The rate MSS achieved for its last similar order was 13.75 stg, 50 pence lower than the fixture before that.
Booker was in the market for 7,800 tonnes from Georgetown to UK/Nantes for 14/18 October and Czarnikow Rionda for 12,000 tonnes in bags from Buenaventura to Sri Lanka for 7/15 October.
Gill & Duffus was open for a prompt 12,000-tonne bagged cargo from Santos to Libya and Louis Dreyfus quoted for 8,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Santos or Paranagua to the Red Sea for 20/25 October.
Two bulk orders reported late on Monday came from Australian shipper CSR and the South Africa Sugar Association (SASA).
CSR quoted for 16,000 min/max from Queensland to Japan for prompt dates and SASA for 18,600 from Durban to the US east coast or Gulf for 1/15 October.

Firmer business included Fiji Sugar Marketing, said to have filled its earlier inquiry for 15,500 tonnes in bulk from Fiji to Japan for 15/20 October and Genoc fixed a prompt 4,000-tonne bagged cargo from Continent to Algeria. Cargill fixed 14,000 tonnes in bulk from north Brazil to Morocco, Egyptian Mediterranean or Black Sea for early October.
